text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bunds rose to strong gains in late trade, boosted by gains in the U.S. debt market amid short-covering ahead of the U.S. December unemployment report due on Friday. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.39, up 0.55 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts made a late bid for higher ground, spurred by a strong start to U.S Treasuries. "The rise was initially fuelled by U.S. producer prices which were not as bad as they seemed," said one trader. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-2/32, up 20/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures got a late boost from strength in the German and U.S. bond markets to break through resistance at 128.42 and reach their highest level this year, but traders said the gains remained fragile. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.74, up 0.52 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets ended with sturdy gains as technical factors and in some cases shortcovering drove them higher. The March bond future on LIFFE was at 128.84, up 0.80 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries rose to session highs at midday, as tame inflation and weak economic news took the market out of its week-long doldrums. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-8/32, up 17/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.78 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures ended the Tokyo session up after a strong 10-year JGB auction, but pared gains somewhat on profit taking fueled in part by a stock market tumble. In after-hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 124.88, up 0.13 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market activity simmered down after a hectic week of issuance. Mexico was due to price a $1.0 billion 10-year bond at 337.5 b.p. over Treasuries. EIB added 500 million marks to its October 2003 bond. Rabobank issued a high-yielding 1.0 billion Czech crown two-year bond.
